tower-of-hanoi.title: Output move list as final answer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After solving the puzzle, present the complete sequence of moves as a single list in the exact format [[disk, from_peg, to_peg], ...]. The answer parser extracts the last parseable list, so any extra text before or after can cause mis‑parsing.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you have generated the full, legal move sequence for the given Tower of Hanoi instance.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Providing explanatory sentences after the list or omitting the list entirely, causing the parser to miss the moves.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Free blocked larger disks by moving top smaller disks first
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the disk you need to move is not on top of its peg, first relocate the smaller disks that sit above it to another peg, respecting the size rule, before moving the larger disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever a target disk is blocked by one or more smaller disks on the same peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move a larger disk while a smaller disk remains on top, resulting in an illegal move.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Consolidate all disks onto a single source peg before applying classic Hanoi recursion
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When the initial configuration spreads disks across several pegs, first move the smaller disks onto the peg that already holds the larger disks, creating a single stack. Once all disks are on one peg, the classic recursive Hanoi algorithm can be applied safely.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: If the starting state is not a single stack on one peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to run the recursive solution while disks are split across pegs, causing illegal moves because the larger disks are not reachable.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate destination peg before each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before moving a disk, check that the destination peg is either empty or its topmost disk is larger than the moving disk; otherwise the move would place a larger disk on a smaller one, violating the rules.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving a larger disk onto a peg where a smaller disk is on top, which is illegal because a larger disk cannot rest on a smaller one.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Keep answer concise and place move list at the very end
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The answer parser reads the last parseable list; any trailing text after the move list can be ignored or cause parsing errors. Therefore, output only the move list and nothing else after it.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Appending a concluding sentence after the move list, which leads the parser to miss the moves.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate source peg before each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Ensure that the disk you intend to move is the topmost disk on its source peg; if a smaller disk blocks it, you must first move that smaller disk elsewhere.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move a larger disk while a smaller disk remains on top of it, resulting in an illegal move.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Apply classic Hanoi recursion to generate move sequence
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Use the recursive pattern: to move n disks from source to target using auxiliary, first recursively move n‑1 disks from source to auxiliary, then move the nth (largest) disk from source to target, and finally recursively move the n‑1 disks from auxiliary to target. This yields a correct sequence for any number of disks.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to transfer a stack of disks from one peg to another (including after consolidating them onto a single peg).
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving the largest disk before moving the smaller disks that block it, which either violates the size rule or leaves the smaller disks unmoved.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may stop generation early or forget to output the moves.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Make sure to generate and include the full move list before ending the answer.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Truncated move list (incomplete solution) due to token limit
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may run out of tokens or stop before completing the sequence.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Plan the solution to fit within token limits, or generate the moves in a compact form to stay within the limit.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a non‑top disk (source peg top mismatch)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may select a disk to move without checking if it is the topmost on its peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Validate that the chosen disk is the topmost on its source peg; if not, move the blocking smaller disks first.
